name: MA-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent seeking re-election in a safe seat
Markets price a Democratic win at ~95%
model.rationale: Trahan is a well-funded incumbent in a district that leans Democratic by 11 points, while Republican Gary Grossi has raised only about $7,000 with no outside spending. Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 95%, and fundamentals point to a margin in the low twenties.
model.watch: Any late surge in Republican outside spending or an unexpected polling shift could narrow the expected margin, though a Republican win remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Lori Trahan seeks re-election in a Massachusetts district that voted Democratic by 11 points more than the nation. She has raised about $1.6 million and holds $1.8 million on hand, while Republican Gary Grossi has raised roughly $7,000. No independent groups have advertised in the race, and no general-election polls are available.

With no expert ratings listed, the picture rests on fundamentals: the district lean, incumbency, and an overwhelming money gap all favor Trahan. Prediction markets put her chances around 95 percent. A low-turnout or wave environment could shift the margin somewhat, but the seat remains firmly in Democratic hands.
